title: Settled Share of the Billing Period in Paloma Business Upgrade Proration
content:
On a Paloma Business upgrade inside a billing period, the share of the period settled depends on the billing cycle and on the days of the period used before the upgrade, counted from the first day of the period up to the day before the upgrade. The unused days run from the upgrade date to the last day of the period, both days included, and the period's days from its first day to its last day, both included.

### Ruling

A monthly-billed account that used three days or fewer settles the whole period, so the share is one; a monthly-billed account that used four to ten days settles the unused days over a 30-day month; every other account settles the unused days over the period's days.

The settled share is the share by which both the higher plan's monthly fee and the subscription charge collected for the current billing period are multiplied in the proration.

### Day-count table

| Billing cycle | Days used before the upgrade | Share settled |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly | 0 to 3 | One, the whole period |
| Monthly | 4 to 10 | Unused days over 30 |
| Monthly | 11 or more | Unused days over the period's days |
| Annual | Any number | Unused days over the period's days |

### Cases (hypothetical period 1 July to 31 July, 31 days)

- Upgrade on 4 July, monthly billing: 1 to 3 July used, 3 days; the share is one.
- Upgrade on 5 July, monthly billing: 4 days used; unused days 5 to 31 July, 27; share 27 over 30, that is 0.9.
- Upgrade on 11 July, monthly billing: 10 days used; unused days 21; share 21 over 30, that is 0.7.
- Upgrade on 12 July, monthly billing: 11 days used; unused days 20; share 20 over 31.
- Upgrade on 3 July, annual billing: share 29 over 31.
